title: Groundwater Monitoring in Wabasha County, MN
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers - St. Paul District is seeking a contractor to perform groundwater monitoring services in support of the Grand Encampment Dredge Material Placement Site Unload project along the Zumbro River near Kellogg, MN in Wabasha County. This solicitation is 100% set-aside for small business under NAICS 541380 with a size standard of $19 million. The contractor will collect water samples from three monitoring wells and up to four government-selected residential wells before, during and after the active unloading of the site in Spring 2027. During the active unload phase samples will also be collected from the river upstream of the site and from standing water within the active dredged-material placement/infiltration pit. Water samples will be analyzed by an environmental analytical testing laboratory accredited under the Minnesota Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (MNELAP) for all specified methods and parameters. Pre-Placement (Phase 1) samples will be collected and tested approximately 90, 60 and 30 days prior to the start of the active hydraulic transfer of stockpiled dredge materials to the upland placement site. Samples will be collected and tested during Active Placement (Phase 2) approximately 3, 17, and 31 days after the transfer begins, with options for additional sample collection and testing at approximately 45, 59 and 73 days after start of transfer. Post-Placement (Phase 3) samples will be collected and tested approximately 30, 60 and 90 days after the completion of the materials transfer. The contractor will prepare a final sampling and analysis report, submitted within 50 days of testing completion. All questions should be submitted in writing via the PIEE module Q and A section. Offers should be submitted via the PIEE Module. Click the first link in the Attachments/Links section.

title: 6515--Reprocessed Non-Critical Single Use Devices
description: THIS IS A COMBINED SYNOPSIS AND SOLICITATION NOTICE OF TIERED EVALUATIONS: This procurement action for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Medical/Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) Supplies Program and is set-aside based on an order of priority as established in 38 U.S.C. 8127. TIERED EVALUATIONS INCLUDING LARGE BUSINESS CONCERNS: This solicitation is being issued as a tiered evaluation with the following tiers: (1) SDVOSB concerns, (2) VOSB concerns, (3) small business concerns with HUBZone small business concerns and 8(a) participants having priority; and (4) large business concerns. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is publishing this Request for Quotes (RFQ) on or about October 30, 2026, for the acquisition of consumable commodities in support of the Medical/Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) Program catalogue. The MSPV Program is a partnering effort between Veterans Healthcare Administration (VHA) and the VA Office of Acquisition, Logistics & Construction (OALC) to deliver a national strategic sourcing solution that combines a formulary approach with electronic cataloging and ordering of a wide range of medical and surgical supplies for the Veterans Administration Medical Centers (VAMC) and related facilities. The establishment of Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) is in direct support of this initiative and is a key element in the success of the MSPV Program, as the BPAs will provide the mechanism that will supply the types of supplies for distribution to all VHA facilities located in the United States (U.S.) and all U.S. Territories. In order to support the MSPV Program, the VA will establish BPAs for medical/surgical supplies through Open Market BPAs under FAR Part 12. This solicitation is structured as a tiered evaluation to maximize Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business and Veteran-Owned Small Business (SD/VOSB) participation. Quotations will be evaluated based on technical criteria and price. VHA clinicians will participate in evaluating all supplier quotations and awards will be made using comparative analysis. In order for an authorized distributor/supplier to participate in the MSPV Program, the authorized distributor/supplier and the Prime Vendor shall establish a Commercial Agreement within 60 days of award. The Commercial Agreement will govern the terms and conditions of the authorized distributor/supplier relationship and will not contradict the underlying terms and conditions established by this BPA or the underlying MSPV Contract. See Statement of Work for further details. The MSPV Program recognizes that various NAICS codes may/can be used for this procurement. The standard/typical NAICS code for surgical/medical supplies manufacturing (not including medical instruments or equipment) is 339113. Any future amendments and other miscellaneous documents will be available electronically for download at the following URL: http://www.sam.gov. No paper copies of the presolicitation/solicitation will be available, and no telephone requests for paper copies of the presolicitation/solicitation will be accepted. Interested Quoters are advised to continuously check the URL for any changes to this solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a quote that, if timely received NLT the due date and time for quote submission, will be given full consideration. MSPV is seeking quotes from authorized sources (including manufacturers) for each of the items on the quote sheet. The quote sheet for submission is found as Attachment A - Quote Sheet_36C24E27Q0005_Reprocessed SUDs_V1 and is the only acceptable quote sheet for submission. NOTE: All items are original equipment manufacturer products, and only the items listed can be quoted. MSPV is NOT seeking like or substitute items. Quotes for items not listed by OEM number on the quote sheet will not be accepted. If an item has been discontinued and a direct replacement is available, please provide that information to the Contracting Officer listed below. Be advised, the Government is not seeking substitute, equivalent, or like items at this time. Only direct replacements for discontinued items will be considered for this solicitation. If an item found within this solicitation classifies as a prosthetic item or is on another national-level VA contract vehicle please advise the Contracting Officer listed below. Any further questions may be directed to the Contracting Officer listed below. All questions and communications shall be in writing to the Contracting Officer at the email address listed below. Any revised/updated information received will be published as an amendment that revises/corrects the quote sheet. It is the burden of the quoter to continuously monitor this solicitation for any subsequent amendments. An Authorized Distributor Letter (ADL) from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) shall be included with all responses. The ADL from the OEM shall include each product(s) proposed authorizing the Quoter as a distributor for the proposed product(s). The letter must either state specific product(s) proposed or that the Quoter is an authorized distributor for all of OEM s products. The letter must expressly state that the Quoter is an authorized distributor for the MSPV BPA Program. This letter must be on the OEM s letterhead and contain the signature of an authorized official for the OEM. Additionally, the letter must be signed and dated within 90 days of the time the Contracting Officer receives it. See the Statement of Work included in the solicitation for further details. A sample ADL is included in this RFQ as Attachment B - Sample Authorized Distributor Letter_36C24E27Q0005 for reference only. Please ensure the verbiage in the ADL includes correct manufacturer and supplier information. See the Statement of Work for specific information regarding the ADL requirement. Completed and accurate quote sheets along with any other required documentation must be timely received no later than 12:00pm EDT on November 18, 2026. Any quote sheets received after this date may not be accepted. title: Personal Radiation Detector (PRD)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) SUMMARY: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Office of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) requires Personal Radiation Detectors (PRDs). PRDs are pager-size devices worn by users for radiological and nuclear detection capability as well as personal protection. PRDs automatically monitor the environment and alert the user when radiation levels above the natural background are detected. PRDs also assist the user in localizing the source of detected radiation. The high sensitivity and rapid response time to the variations in the ambient radiation levels clearly distinguish PRDs from the family of electronic dosimeters which are mainly used for accurate dose and dose rate. GENERAL INFORMATION: This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify offerors that can provide identify commercially available, gamma-detecting Personal Radiation Detectors (PRDs), including available wireless-communication and data-transmission capabilities in advance of an acquisition which will include testing of the most compliant candidate solutions. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. Interested parties must submit sufficient documentation in accordance with the instructions in this RFI and current industry�s best practices and standards, demonstrating their ability/experience to meet or exceed the Government�s requirements listed in this notice. RFI RESPONSE SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS: Interested contractors shall submit their RFI responses electronically to Isaac Chapple, Contracting Officer, at Isaac.Chapple@fema.dhs.gov no later than 12:00PM Eastern Standard Time (EST), (due 11/18/2026).

title: Sources Sought - Procurement of New or Overhauled UC-12W PT6A-60A Turboprop Engine
description: Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of the Tactical Airlift Program Office (PMA-207), is conducting market research to identify responsible and qualified sources capable of furnishing PT6A-60A turboprop engines in either new production condition or overhauled condition meeting original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specifications and all applicable airworthiness, configuration-control, inspection, test, preservation, and technical-data requirements. The Government is seeking information from qualified vendors to include the OEM, OEM-authorized distributors, OEM-authorized maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) providers, and other responsible sources capable of supplying PT6A-60A engines for military aviation application. The Government seeks to identify potential business sources with the resources, capabilities, and experience necessary for the procurement of a PT6A-60A turboprop engine; and to obtain estimated procurement costs. Requested Industry Information: Interested sources are requested to submit a capabilities statement addressing the following: 1. Company Information Company name, address, CAGE code, UEI, and business-size status; Primary point of contact, telephone number, and email address; Identification of the respondent as OEM, authorized distributor, authorized MRO provider, or other source. 2. Technical Capability Demonstrated experience supplying new or overhauled PT6A-60A engines; Evidence of OEM authorization, distributorship, repair-station authorization, or other relevant qualification; Description of facilities, quality-management system, test-cell capability, and technical personnel; Description of the respondent�s configuration-control and parts-traceability processes; Ability to provide required engine records, airworthiness documentation, and certification documentation; Description of warranty terms and post-delivery technical support. 3.Schedule and Capacity Estimated lead time for new production engines; Estimated lead time for overhauled engines; Current and projected production/overhaul capacity; Identification of supply-chain risks, long-lead components, or other schedule constraints. 4. Commerciality and Pricing Information Whether the offered engine is customarily used by the general public or nongovernmental entities for purposes other than governmental purposes; Whether the item is sold competitively in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace; Rough-order-of-magnitude pricing or commercial catalog/pricelist information, if available; Separate estimated pricing for new production and overhauled engines, if applicable; Recommended contract type, ordering approach, and warranty structure. 5. Small Business Participation Identification of any small-business teaming, subcontracting, distribution, overhaul, logistics, or sustainment capabilities relevant to this requirement; Recommendations for structuring a future acquisition to maximize competition and small-business participation, where practicable. Response Instructions: Responses should be submitted electronically in PDF format no later than 12:00 p.m. on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, to: Katelyn Campbell katelyn.e.campbell4.civ@us.navy.mil The email subject line shall read: "Sources Sought Response � PT6A-60A Turboprop Engine � [Company Name]" Respondents should clearly identify any proprietary information. The Government will use submitted information only for market-research and acquisition-planning purposes, consistent with applicable handling requirements. Disclaimer: This sources sought notice is for informational and planning purposes only. It shall not be construed as a solicitation, request for quote, request for proposal, obligation, or commitment by the Government to procure any supplies or services. The Government reserves the right to revise or discontinue this effort at any time.

title: Coburn Gore LPOE Art in Architecture Project
description: Document Added & Updated: 0332CG-AIA- Coburn Gore AIA Questions & Answers V3 Dated 07 October 2026 The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents or Permanent Workers of the United States) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal buildings nationwide. GSA announces an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Coburn Gore Land Port of Entry (LPOE) in Coburn, Maine. The new facility will strengthen supply chains, improve operational capabilities and facility infrastructure, spur economic growth, and bolster the country�s security. The project will provide a fully operational LPOE that coordinates with the tra?c ?ow and operations of the Canadian port of entry at Saint-Augustin-de-Woburn Quebec, Port of Entry. The project will provide a new port that allows Customs and Border Protection to more efficiently carry out its agency mission, their operations and interactions with the public. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $275,000 to $400,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: https://www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the LPOE in Coburn Gore, ME must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 12:00 PM Eastern Time on 18 November 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. At minimum, the scope of services for this commission will require collaboration with the lead designer selected for the land port of entry project; travel to the project site; development and presentation of preliminary and final concepts; fabrication of the artwork; participation in meetings and conservation reviews as necessary; delivery and installation of the artwork; professional documentation of, and detailed maintenance planning for the artwork at the project site. For informational purposes: Artists selected for the contract award must be Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of award. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 13934, agencies should prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded. Inquiries concerning the project should be directed to the following email address: Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov and reference the synopsis number in the subject line. No questions will be answered after 07 October 2026 12:00pm EST.

title: End of the World Long Term Stewardship
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26R4016 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the End of the World G-Z Long-Term IRSC (EOTW G-Z LTIRSC). The End of the World Project area is approximately 50,000 acres on the Salmon River Ranger District of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest. The End of the World EIS authorizes commercial treatment on over 17,000 acres primarily through intermediate harvest. The purpose of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to thin overstocked stands to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire as well as improve stand health. The EOTW Project is within the Wildland Urban Interface and has numerous private inholdings with seasonal and permanent residents. This contracting tool will increase the pace and scale of active management beyond the current capacity of staffing levels. A secondary objective of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to provide a steady, dependable supply of timber and forest products to local facilities. This project aligns with Secretarial Memo 1078-006 and the Implementation of Secretarial Memo 1078-006 dated April 3, 2025 to utilize long term stewardship contracts for active management. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 113310 and the small business size standard is 500 Employees This acquisition is an unrestricted requirement. All responsible sources may submit a proposal and offer which will be considered by the agency. Proposals are to be submitted via email to Mark Phillipp at mark.phillipp@usda.gov and Matt Daigle at matthew.daigle@usda.gov.

description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution (FCI) McKean, Bradford, Pennsylvania, herein issues solicitation 15B20927Q00000003 for the requirements of: TRASH REMOVAL AND HAULING SERVICES. This solicitation is restricted, 100% Small Business. Services are expected to begin DECEMBER 1, 2026 and run through SEPTEMBER 30th, 2027. Services will take place at FCI McKean, 6975 Route 59, Lewis Run, PA 16738, 15 Miles South of Bradford, PA. The contract type is a firm-fixed price. The Government reserves the right upon award to make formal single or multiple awards. The Government will award the responsible offerors whose bid, conforming to the solicitation, are considered to be most advantageous to the Government, with both past performance and price considered. The solicitation will be available on October 30th, 2026 at 11:30 AM EST and will be posted to the General Services Administration Federal Business Opportunities website: www.sam.gov/. All future information about this acquisition, including solicitation amendments, will be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure they have the most up-to-date information about this solicitation. All contractors doing business with the Federal Government shall be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database. The website for registration is: www.sam.gov. The closing date for receipt of quotes is November 18TH, 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. Payment will be made using Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) through a purchase order. Faith-based and community-based organizations have the right to submit offers/quotes equally with other organizations for contracts for which they are eligible. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 562111. The point of contact for all information regarding this solicitation is Cory Sudbrook, Supervisory Contract Specialist, telephone number (814)-362-8900 extension 3419 and Alyssa McGrew, Contract Specialist, at the address listed below and telephone number (814) 362-8900, extension 3422. Completed offers must be emailed to amcgrew@bop.gov and csudbrook@bop.gov or faxed to (814) 363-6815. Emails are preferred. If you do not receive a confirmation email, please call to verify. The anticipated award date is November 20th, 2026.

title: Automated Ultrasound-Based, Super Intelligence (SI)-Enabled Fracture Detection
description: The Center for Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) intends to use responses to this Sources Sought Notice (SSN) for planning purposes. BARDA will not award any contracts under this Notice, but rather seeks current and forecasted prices, inventories, capabilities, and other pertinent marketplace data. This Notice is issued by the Center for Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) to identify innovative medical countermeasure technologies to enable rapid triage of musculoskeletal injuries such as fractures and soft tissue injuries of extremities. This request is for information only and is intended to assess the current state of commercially available technologies and technologies nearing commercial availability that support automated ultrasound-based fracture detection using technologies commonly known as Artificial Intelligence (AI). Consistent with Executive Order 14434, �Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence,� AI- technologies are now referred to as Super Intelligence (SI) throughout this notice, including in the title and should be referred the same in the response. The Center for Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) intends to use responses to this Sources Sought Notice (SSN) to inform planning for the potential acquisition of ultrasound-based devices capable of capturing and displaying anatomical data. Potential acquisition and inventory approaches include device purchases or leases supported by vendor-managed inventory (VMI) arrangements. BARDA seeks information on technologies that could assist clinical care providers in visualizing or detecting musculoskeletal injuries, including fractures and soft tissue injuries, to support triage and initial treatment in emergency departments, urgent care centers, and field settings. These devices could also support continued evaluation and treatment in definitive orthopedic care settings, consistent with applicable regulatory authorizations and intended uses. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) leads Federal public health and medical preparedness and response efforts, including supporting the research, development, acquisition, and availability of medical countermeasures (MCMs). These efforts address the health consequences of chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) threats, pandemic influenza, and emerging infectious diseases, including threats arising from deliberate, accidental, or naturally occurring events. This SSN supports planning for medical capabilities that could strengthen the Nation�s preparedness for and response to emergencies involving traumatic injuries. The Project BioShield Act of 2004 (Pub. L. No. 108-276) established authorities for procuring qualifying security countermeasures for the Strategic National Stockpile (SNS). The Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness Act of 2006 (Pub. L. No. 109-417) further strengthened the Nation�s medical countermeasure development and preparedness framework. The National Health Security Strategy 2023�2026 provides additional strategic context for strengthening preparedness, response, and recovery capabilities. Consistent with these preparedness objectives, this Sources Sought Notice seeks information on potential approaches to improve the availability and accessibility of relevant medical devices across health care settings. Approaches of interest include purchase, lease, vendor-managed inventory (VMI), and arrangements that combine access to devices with maintenance and readiness support. Information received will inform acquisition planning and assessment of these approaches, subject to applicable statutory authorities, acquisition requirements, and availability of funds. These documents represent the foundation for addressing the Nation�s CBRN MCM needs. Amongst the foundational documents referenced above, musculoskeletal injuries such as fractures resulting from nuclear blast explosions and structural collapse, as well as and other mass casualty events present significant challenges in both field and clinical settings which require prompt diagnosis for adjudication and triage of patients. Current standards of care rely heavily on radiography and CT imaging, which are often unavailable, delayed, or resource-constrained in austere environments, disaster response settings, or during patient surge conditions. Delayed or missed fracture diagnosis can worsen patient outcomes and burden downstream care. BARDA is seeking solutions that enhance the speed, accuracy, and accessibility of fracture detection at the point of injury and point of care, without dependence on traditional imaging infrastructure. CAPABILITY STATEMENT/INFORMATION SOUGHT This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) seeks information from small business (SB) and other than small business (OTSB) concerns regarding their qualifications, experience, and capabilities to develop, manufacture, and deploy standalone, point-of-care, super intelligence (SI)-enabled ultrasound devices for fracture detection. Respondents shall provide only the information, data, and materials necessary to demonstrate their capabilities relevant to this notice. Responses shall include separate Technical Representation and Business Representation sections, as detailed below. Each section shall not exceed 10 single-sided pages, including all attachments, r�sum�s, charts, and other supporting materials, and shall use 12-point Times New Roman font. Pages exceeding the limit for either section will not be reviewed. Respondents shall identify their business size status as either small business or other than small business under the NAICS code and corresponding size standard identified in this notice. Technical Representations Respondents shall provide the technical information requested by ASPR/BARDA in separately numbered sections, in the order listed below. For any section that does not apply, respondents shall retain the section number and heading, mark it �Not Applicable,� and briefly explain why it does not apply. Response Specification In response to this notice, clearly describe the capability and experience that meets the criteria specified in the subsequent categories. A template is provided for detailed and concise responses as related to the qualifying criteria. Additional supporting evidence, data, and information can be provided as attachments, not to exceed the 10-page limit per submission to this notice. All sponsors responding to this notice are required to provide the requested information on their products and capabilities by providing short responses, summarizing their device's diagnostic capability along with performance data, TRL and development status, regulatory documentation, product IFU, manufacturing overview, and supply-chain and production information. The narrative response to the templated prompts may include figures, schematics, diagrams, photographs, etc. and shall describe the proposed final product under consideration. Any proposed device must qualify against the following criteria (either work completed or demonstratable work in progress): Display and Diagnostic of Anatomy for Fracture Evaluation Capability Automated ultrasound imaging-based volumetric capture and display of detailed anatomy of different structures and providing bone detection/identification in areas such as wrist, ankles and others; and assist care providers to visualize clinically significant injuries such as fractures. Embedded ultrasound image processing information with appropriately trained Super Intelligence and machine learning (SI/ML) models to assist in image acquisition and segmentation for data interpretation with predefined sensitivity/specificity performance, which has been reviewed and adjudicated in FDA submissions for 510k clearance process. Models must be rigorously tested/validated against independent datasets separate from their training and their performance must improve upon that of human imaging

title: Kingdom of Bahrain S&RTS
description: 13 November 2026: Extend the due date to 18 November 2026 @ 12:00PM CST 10 November 2026: MFR re solicitation number 06 November 2026: Update Addendum to FAR 52.212-1 with correct quote due date of 13 November 2026. 04 November 2026: P0003 Revised SOR. 27 October 2026: P0002 Updated PWS dated 27 October 2026. Post Round 1-3 Q&A's. 23 October 2026: P0001 Extend the due date to 13 November 2026. **Please take note that the solicitation number has been updated to HTC71127QE127 due to overlap in Fiscal Years** The purpose of this requirement is to provide S&RTS in connection with the import and export of designated U.S. Government (USG) cargo throughout the Kingdom of Bahrain. Primary performance locations include Mina Salman Port, Khalifa Bin Salman Port, ASRY Dry Dock, Naval Support Activity (NSA1), Mina Salman Naval Base (NSA2), Shaikh Isa Air Base, Aviation Unit (NSA3), Riffa Air Base and any other designated locations within Kingdom of Bahrain. S&RTS services will cover the full spectrum of managing USG cargo (e.g. containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and rotary or fixed wing aircraft) transiting through the specified port(s) in this contract. Operational tasks shall include but are not limited to stevedoring and long-shoring services required to conduct and facilitate load and discharge of vessel, truck, port reception and disposition, cargo management and preparation, staging, storage, onward movement, intra-port transfers, vessel preparation, documentation, tallying and checking, and storage of dunnage and tiedown materials. Military cargo may consist of vehicles, Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) in all sizes and configurations (containerized or breakbulk), non-explosive containers of all sizes, all classes of Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT) (IAW applicable regulations), and other general DoW cargo. Transportation will be facilitated via vessel, Common-User Land Transportation (CULT), and/or military convoy.

title: Advanced Marksmanship, Close-Quarters Tactics (CQT), and Visit, Board, Search, and Seizure (VBSS) Training Course
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is issued solely for information, market research, and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This RFI does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. All information received in response to this RFI will be considered for informational purposes only. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future solicitation, if one is issued. 1.0 Purpose The Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune Contracting Office, on behalf of 2d Reconnaissance Battalion (2d Recon), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to conduct market research under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 611699, All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction, with a small-business size standard of $16.5 million in average annual receipts. The Government is seeking to identify qualified small-business and other-than-small-business vendors capable of providing Advanced Marksmanship, Close-Quarters Tactics (CQT), and Visit, Board, Search, and Seizure (VBSS) in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). The purpose of this RFI is to assess the availability, capability, capacity, and socioeconomic status of potential sources; obtain industry feedback on the draft requirement; and support development of an appropriate acquisition strategy. 2.0 Background & Technical Requirements 2d Reconnaissance Battalion (2d Recon) requires contractor support to provide Advanced Marksmanship, Close-Quarters Tactics (CQT), and Visit, Board, Search, and Seizure (VBSS) Training in accordance with the attached PWS. The anticipated requirement includes, but is not limited to: Planning, coordinating, developing, and delivering required training or instructional services; Providing qualified instructors, facilitators, subject-matter experts, and support personnel, as required; Developing or furnishing lesson plans, training materials, student guides, practical exercises, and other instructional materials; Coordinating with Government personnel on training schedules, locations, class sizes, equipment, safety requirements, and student prerequisites; Performing training at [insert place(s) of performance] or other Government-designated locations; Providing attendance rosters, student evaluations, after-action reports, and other deliverables identified in the PWS; and Complying with all quality-control, safety, credentialing, administrative, and performance requirements stated in the PWS. 3.0 Required Vendor Response To assist the Government in determining the availability of qualified small businesses and finalizing our acquisition strategy, interested vendors are requested to submit a brief capability package answering the following questions: Corporate Capability and Relevant Experience Describe the firm�s experience providing training, instructional, facilitation, or related services comparable in scope, complexity, and operational environment to the requirement described in the PWS. Include up to three relevant examples of current or recent efforts. Technical Capability Describe the firm�s ability to perform the PWS requirements, including: Availability of qualified instructors, facilitators, and subject-matter experts; Relevant instructor qualifications, certifications, licenses, and experience; Capability to develop, tailor, maintain, and deliver training materials; Ability to meet anticipated scheduling, class-size, throughput, and delivery-location requirements; Quality-control processes for instructor performance and training delivery; and Ability to meet specialized equipment, facility, safety, travel, logistical, or administrative requirements. Staffing and Surge Capacity Describe the firm�s proposed staffing approach and its ability to accommodate changes in student throughput, training frequency, delivery locations, or other mission requirements. Identify anticipated subcontracting, personnel, equipment, or facility constraints. Quality Assurance and Past Performance Describe the firm�s quality-assurance program, including methods for monitoring instructor performance, assessing student feedback and training effectiveness, documenting corrective actions, and ensuring compliance with contractual requirements. Business Size and Socioeconomic Status State the firm�s business size under NAICS 611699 and identify all applicable socioeconomic designations, including, as applicable: Small Business; Small Disadvantaged Business; 8(a) Program Participant; Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business; Historically Underutilized Business Zone Small Business; Woman-Owned Small Business; and/or Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business. Contracting Vehicles Identify any active Federal Supply Schedules, Governmentwide Acquisition Contracts, Blanket Purchase Agreements, Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity contracts, or other available contract vehicles that could support this requirement. Industry Feedback Provide recommendations or concerns regarding the PWS, including: Ambiguous, incomplete, duplicative, or unnecessarily restrictive requirements; Recommended revisions that may improve competition or performance outcomes; Suggested contract type, pricing structure, ordering structure, or period of performance; Recommended performance metrics or quality-assurance measures; and Anticipated risks related to staffing, scheduling, travel, facilities, equipment, or instructional delivery. 4.0 Submission Instructions Responses to this RFI must be submitted via email to the Contract Administrators listed below no later than 18 November 2026 at 1:00 PM EST. Sgt. Elijah D. Hillsgrove Email: elijah.hillsgrove@usmc.mil Phone: 910-451-1286 SSgt. Lucas B. Elliot Email: lucas.elliott@usmc.mil Phone: 910-450-7532

description: SPECIAL NOTICE: VENDORS MUST REFERENCE THE NOTICE ID WHEN SUBMITTING A CAPABILITY STATEMENT. NASA/NSSC has a requirement for A one-year production engagement between NASA and Earthmover. It builds on the MERRA-21C cloud-native pilot that ran from April to June 2026. NASA/NSSC intends to issue a sole source contract to Earthmover PBC under the authority of FAR 12.102(a). It has been determined that Earthmover PBC is the sole provider of A one-year production engagement between NASA and Earthmover. It builds on the MERRA-21C cloud-native pilot that ran from April to June 2026. NASA/NSSC will be the procuring center for this effort. Performance will be located at NASA/ Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC). The Government intends to acquire Commercial items or services using the provisions, clauses and procedures prescribed in FAR Part 12 for Commercial The NAICS Code for this procurement is 518210. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort in writing to the identified point of contact not later than 12:00 p.m. Central Standard Time on 11/18/2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed effort on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. NOTE: Quotes received in response to this notice will NOT be considered and will not be evaluated by NASA�s Technical End User Team. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. This Sources Sought is only for the purpose of identifying potential sources and alternative products as part of 181st Intelligence Wing, IN ANG market research. No Solicitation exists; therefore, do not request a copy. As part of its market research, 181 MSG/MSC is issuing this Sources Sought to determine if there exist an adequate number of qualified interested contractors capable of providing the requirement. The Government may use the responses to this Sources Sought for information and planning purposes. The 181st IW has two fiber lines running through a manhole that need to be spliced to restore connectivity to one of our buildings. Due to the existing conditions, the contractor would need to have personnel who are qualified and equipped to enter the manhole/confined space, access the existing fiber, pull or work with the available slack, and complete the required fiber splicing and testing. Identify a company that can perform both the confined-space/manhole work and the fiber splicing.

title: Z1DA--550-20-121 Demo Old Boiler Plant B100 (CON)
description: Presolicitation Notice Presolicitation Notice Page 3 of 3 Presolicitation Notice *=Required Field Presolicitation Notice Page 1 of 3 PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE This notice does NOT constitute a request for proposal, request for quote or invitation for bid. Solicitation: 36C25227B0002 Project: 550-20-121: Demo Old Boiler Plant B100 (CON) Location: VA Illiana Health Care System (VAIHCS) 1900 East Main Street Danville, IL 61832 VA Illiana Health Care System (VAIHCS) has a requirement to demolish old boiler plant in Building 100 in accordance with the project drawings and specifications. Work includes general construction, demolition, removal of underground storage tank, traditional asbestos abatement, lead-based paint removal and disposal, and certain other items. Contractor shall Furnish all labor, materials, supplies, equipment, tools, supervision, management, and all other necessary resources required for Project #550-20-121 Demo Old Boiler Plant B100 as required by the drawings and specifications. The Period of Performance is One Hundred Eighty (180) calendar days from the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The NTP shall be issued approximately 14 calendar days after award once required payment and performance bonds and certificate of insurance is provided. The solicitation, specifications and drawings will be posted on www.SAM.gov. There will be a pre-bid conference held for this project and all prospective bidders are strongly encouraged to attend. Details of the pre-bid conference will be included in the solicitation package. Pursuant to Public Law 109-461, this solicitation is set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) firms. In accordance with VAAR 819.7003(DEVIATION) (b), at the time of submission of bids, and at the time of award of any contract, the offeror must represent to the CO that it is a (1) SDVOSB eligible under VAAR Subpart 819.70; (2) Small business concern under the NAICS code assigned to this acquisition; and (3) Certified SDVOSB listed in the SBA certification database at https://veterans.certify.sba.gov/ (see 13 CFR 128). The solicitation will be issued on or about October 8, 2026. The bidder is responsible for monitoring and downloading any amendments from SAM.gov which may be issued to this solicitation. The magnitude of the requirement is between $1,000,000.00 and $2,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification Code (NAICS) for this procurement is 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction; small business $45 Million size standard applies.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source the Co-sponsorship of a Forum on Traumatic Brain Injury with the National Academies of Science, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM)
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) intends to issue a sole source award. The Defense Health Agency, Science and Technology Portfolio Management Division (STPMD) will co-sponsor a Forum on Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) hosted by the National Academy of Science, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM). The forum will provide STPMD on ongoing mechanism and neutral setting in which the full spectrum of Government stakeholders and public and private sector Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to explore opportunities for collective action directed towards advancement in TBI care and research. The requirement contains a base year plus 4 option years. The NASEM will convene the Forum on TBI two (2) to three (3) times per year to provide and ongoing mechanism and neutral setting in which the full spectrum of Government stakeholders and public and private sector SMEs will share information and explore opportunities for collective action addressing contemporary topics in TBI and research. Forum members will address short- and long-term strategic planning for advancing TBI care and research spanning the full TBI continuum from prevention through acute care and rehabilitation. NASEM has established these forums as part of contract W81XWH22C0033. DHA is planning to participate as a key stakeholder. STPMD requires access to these Forums along with other military services and federal agencies. Any firm that believes it can provide the stated capability as outlined above are invited to submit a written notification to the Contracting Office NLT 2PM ET on 18 November 2026. Supporting evidence must be furnished in sufficient detail to demonstrate the firm�s ability to provide the stated capability. Information shall be sent electronically (via e-mail only) to Rich Trunnell, Contract Specialist, at richard.k.trunnell.civ@health.mil. No telephone requests will be accepted. Responses received will be evaluated; however; a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no responses are received, DHACA will proceed with the sole sources contract.

NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

6632--Cath Lab GEM 5000
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6, intends to negotiate a sole source contract with WERFEN USA LLC for Blood Gas Analyzer (1) GEM Premier 5000 analyzer as Reagent Rental for Cardiac Cath Lab at Durham VAMC. Component Description Analyzer 1 GEM Premier 5000 Data Management GEMWEB Plus 500 System Product GEM PAKs Consumables Solution, Paper Printer Warranty 12 months standard; 48 months extended included The GEM Premier 5000 system is a fully automated blood gas Co-Oximeter/hematocrit/electrolyte/glucose/lactate analyzer used in both the laboratory and the operating room to rapidly analyze pH, pCO2, PO2, Ca2+, Na2+, K+, lactate, glucose, and hematocrit from whole blood. The analyzer features iQM2 with Intraspect technology, which provides real-time quality assurance with every sample analysis continuously. The iQM2 performs checks on samples before, during, and after analysis. This real-time quality assurance feature allows for immediate, automatic correction and automatic documentation. The self-contained GEM PAK does not require refrigeration; this all-in-one PAK performs both the analysis and the Intraspect checks, which can detect errors in sample analysis. The blood gas analyzer measures oxygen, carbon dioxide, and pH in a patient to assess metabolic or respiratory status. The Cardiac Cath Lab requires the acquisition of one (1) new GEM Premier 5000 Blood Gas Analyzer to support testing needs. The instrument will be interfaced with the VA VistA hospital information system. Reference values for blood gas parameters will be established upon installation. title: FLEXIBLE RUBBER PIPE COUPLINGS
description: Solicitation Modification 002: This amendment establishes the pre-award ship-check and field measurement requirements, clarifies the award consideration during technical evaluation, and the missing additional FAR clauses and provisions. 1. Pre-Award Ship Check and Field Measurements The Government does not possess reliable existing measurements; therefore, the performance requirement remains valid. Accordingly, offerors shall complete a ship check and conduct the necessary field measurements specified in the SOW, no later than November 16th, 2026, prior to the solicitation closing date of November 18th, 2026. This includes visually inspecting each of the twenty-four (24) target locations, verifying face-to-face dimensions, flange drilling patterns, allowable lateral/axial movement, adjacent clearances, and piping alignment necessary for off-site fabrication. Due to operational commitments and cutter availability, post-award access for obtaining measurements will not be feasible. Offerors are responsible for coordinating and completing any necessary ship check and field measurements before the established deadline to ensure their proposals are accurate and technically compliant. Requiring completion during the established availability window mitigates fabrication inaccuracies, improper fitting, schedule delays, and performance risk associated with the required delivery date of April 12, 2027. 2. Technical Evaluation and Award Eligibility Completion of the pre-award ship check and field measurements is a mandatory technical acceptability requirement. Offerors shall provide documentation of the completed site visit a technical approach, and technical capability demonstrating that their proposed offer is based on verified measurements meeting the SOW requirements. As previously stated, Firm Fixed Price Proposals shall be detailed and include information from the SOW demonstrating an understanding of all the requirements in the SOW. Proposals that fail to demonstrate compliance with this requirement by the established deadline will be determined technically unacceptable and ineligible for award, regardless of price. 3. Required Delivery Date The RDD remains on or before April 12, 2027. Offerors shall demonstrate their ability to fabricate and deliver the required components within the timeframe based on the verified ship-check measurements and anticipatory delivery date. 4. Additional FAR clauses and provisions. The original solicitation mentioned additional FAR clauses and provisions that was identified as missing. These have been included in an attachment as previously stated. All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. The solicitation closing date and time of 18 November 2026 at 3:00 P.M. Eastern Standard Time remain unchanged. It is the responsibility of interested vendors to monitor the solicitation for any amendments, modifications, or other changes. title: Governor Control Programming
description: Amendment 0002 is issued to extend the Request for Quotation due date from 6 November 2026 to 18 November 2026, 12:00 PM PST and revise the period of performance start dates. Amendment 0001 is issued to extend the Request for Quotation due date from 2 November 2026 to 6 November 2026, 12:00 PM PST. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) at the Libby Dam Project (17877 Hwy 37, Libby, MT 59923) is modernizing its Main Unit Governors by replacing existing pressure switches with pressure transducers on five (5) units. The objective of this contract is to procure specialized governor control programming, Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) / Human Machine Interface (HMI) development, and commissioning support from the contractor to accommodate this hardware change. This is a turnkey requirement; the Contractor assumes full responsibility for understanding the existing system logic and delivering a fully functional, updated programming solution with no technical assistance from the Government. Work shall be accomplished on a rolling outage basis as units become available, spanning from the Contract Award Date through August 30, 2027. Work will occur across remote and on-site location, structured as follows: Tasks 1 & 3 (Remote): Contractor's Facility. Air Combat Command A5 requirements provide for an over-arching sustainment program for the U-2. The Contract Logistics Support (CLS) includes engineering support, the repair of spare assets, resolution of system failures and issues to ensure availability, reliability, and maintainability of the fielded equipment and software. Air Combat Command A5 requirements provide for an over-arching sustainment program for the U-2. The Contract Logistics Support (CLS) includes engineering support, the repair of spare assets, resolution of system failures and issues to ensure availability, reliability, and maintainability of the fielded equipment and software. title: S299--FY27 Pharmaceutical Reverse Distribution Services
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE PHARMACEUTICAL REVERSE DISTRIBUTION SERVICES ORLANDO VA HEALTH CARE SYSTEM (OVAHCS) Notice Type: Sources Sought (Market Research) Notice ID: 36C24827Q0037 Agency: Department of Veterans Affairs Contracting Office: Network Contracting Office 8 (NCO 8) Issuing Office Address: Orlando VA Healthcare System, 13800 Veterans Way, Orlando, FL 32827 NAICS Code: 562119 Size Standard: 250 Employees Product/Service Code: S299 Housekeeping Other Place of Performance: Multiple sites within OVAHCS (Orlando, Daytona Beach, and Viera, FL) Response Due Date: November 18, 2026, 3:00 PM 1. DISCLAIMER THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation announcement, a request for proposals, a request for quotes, or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not pay for any information provided in response to this notice or for the Government's use of such information. All costs associated with responding to this Sources Sought are solely at the responder's expense. The purpose of this notice is to conduct market research to identify qualified sources including Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (VOSB), and other small business categories capable of providing the services described herein. Responses will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy, including potential small business set-aside determinations under FAR Part 19 and 38 U.S.C. §§ 8127 8128 (VA Rule of Two). 2. BACKGROUND The Orlando VA Health Care System (OVAHCS) is required by federal regulation to remove all controlled and non-controlled substances that are expired, recalled, or otherwise determined to be unusable from active stock. These substances must be stored separately until destroyed, reverse distributed, or transferred to a DEA-licensed vendor for destruction, in accordance with 21 CFR Part 1317. OVAHCS is seeking to expand its current destruction-only capability to include pharmaceutical reverse distribution services for non-controlled substances that would otherwise result in lost manufacturer credit opportunities and incomplete inventory lifecycle control, while maintaining destruction capability for both controlled and non-controlled medications across all OVAHCS sites. The intended outcomes include: Recovery of financial credit for eligible non-controlled medications that are reverse distributed. Improved inventory management and reduced waste. Full lifecycle accountability for all medications. Strengthened compliance with VA, DEA, and federal requirements. 3. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Government is seeking a contractor licensed by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) to provide flat-fee services to collect, transport, reverse distribute, and/or destroy controlled (Schedules I V) and non-controlled medications at OVAHCS facilities. Fees shall not be calculated as a percentage of credit returns under any circumstances. 3.1 Scope Highlights The Contractor shall provide: On-site processing of Schedule I V controlled substances and non-controlled substances (including expired, recalled, due-to-expire, or otherwise unusable medications). A minimum of four (4) on-site visits per calendar year at the Outpatient Clinics and Orlando VA Medical Center, with additional visits as directed by the COR. Response within ten (10) business days of a COR request. All shipping instructions, forms, labels, postage, DEA-approved tamper-proof pouches, and boxes required for shipment to the Contractor's central processing facility. Chain-of-custody documentation, including DEA Form 41 for controlled substances, signed by the Pharmacist, Accountable Officer, and Contractor representative. Manufacturer return coordination, credit reconciliation, and Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) compliance. A toll-free (800) number and a web-based service request ordering system. A web-based reporting portal that captures collection date, site, drug name, formulation/strength, NDC, quantity, manufacturer, estimated return value, actual return value, and status of each reverse distribution pickup. Initial orientation and training on all applicable reports and web-based systems. A written Substance Collection Plan and Substance Contingency Plan. 3.2 Applicable Regulatory Framework The Contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including but not limited to: Controlled Substances Act (CSA) 21 CFR Part 1317 (DEA regulations for disposal of controlled substances) Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) 21 CFR (Food & Drugs), 29 CFR (Hazardous Materials), 40 CFR (Environment), 49 CFR (Transportation) EPA, OSHA, FDA, DEA requirements 41 U.S.C. Chapter 67 (Service Contract Labor Standards) All applicable VA policies and facility-specific security requirements 3.3 Places of Performance Facility Address City State ZIP Orlando VAMC at Lake Nona Inpatient 13800 Veterans Way Orlando FL 32827 Orlando VAMC at Lake Nona Outpatient 13800 Veterans Way Orlando FL 32827 Lake Baldwin VA Clinic 5201 Raymond Street Orlando FL 32803 Daytona Beach VA Clinic 1776 North Williamson Blvd Daytona Beach FL 32117 Viera VA Clinic 2900 Veterans Way Viera FL 32940 3.4 Historical Collection Frequency Orlando VAMC at Lake Nona (Inpatient & Outpatient): Monthly Lake Baldwin VA Clinic: Monthly to Quarterly Daytona Beach VA Clinic: Monthly to Quarterly Viera VA Clinic: Monthly to Quarterly Historically each site received approximately 4 12 collection visits per year. Per-shipment weight data is not available. 3.5 Anticipated Period of Performance One (1) base year plus two (2) 12-months option periods, anticipated award date is approximately December 2026. Actual periods will be established in the resulting solicitation. 4. INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM RESPONDENTS Interested and capable sources are requested to submit a capabilities statement not to exceed ten (10) pages (excluding certifications and licensing documentation), addressing the following: 4.1 Company Information Company name, address, point of contact (name, title, phone, email), and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 424210 (Size Standard: 250 employees). Identify all applicable categories: Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) verified in SBA VetCert Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) verified in SBA VetCert Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) / EDWOSB HUBZone Small Business 8(a) Certified Small Business Other than Small Confirmation of active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov). 4.2 Technical Capability Provide a narrative describing the respondent's ability to fulfil the requirement, addressing at minimum: Current DEA registrant status (Schedules II V) and copies of all applicable DEA registrations. Federal, state, local licenses and permits that are held for the interstate transport, storage, and destruction of controlled and non-controlled hazardous and non-hazardous pharmaceuticals (DEA, DOT, EPA, FDA, OSHA, and applicable state authorities). Description of the respondent's central processing/destruction facility, including environmental and hazardous waste compliance systems. Approach to on-site collection, chain of custody, DEA Form 41 processing, and packaging. Description of the web-based service request ordering system and reporting portal, including reconciliation capabilities for expected vs. received credits. Manufacturer return coordination and credit reconciliation approach, including how credits are routed to the Prime Vendor or the VA. DSCSA compliance approach. Approach to responding within ten (10) business days of a COR service request. 4.3 Past Performance Provide up to two (2) examples of similar work (federal, state, or commercial) performed within the last five (5) ye

title: 6505--Nitroglycerin Patches
description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The VA National Acquisition Center intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) 36E79727R0010 for an unrestricted procurement for Nitroglycerin Patches, for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) (inclusive of Consolidated Mail Order Pharmacies (CMOPs) and Option 2 State Veterans Homes (SVH)), Department of Defense (DoD), Bureau of Prisons (BOP), Indian Health Service (IHS), and Federal Health Care Center (FHCC). VA will award one contract to the responsible offeror who will be able to provide an uninterrupted source of supply for the contracted items. The contract period will be for one year plus four pre-priced one-year option periods. The contract items will be distributed through the VA s and DoD s respective Pharmaceutical Prime Vendor Programs. Offerors must state the exact name (name that appears on label) by which the drug will be supplied and have an NDC number that is unique to the offeror. The successful offeror/contractor's label with its unique NDC shall be the only label on the product. Contractors shall not affix their label over another label on the product. VA labels must be able to securely adhere over the successful offeror/contractor's label. This product does not require unit of use packaging, as identified in the Schedule of Supplies. Patches must be boxed and must contain the bar code. The outside box as well as the patch must be barcoded. Solicitation #36E79727R0010 will be electronically issued in commercial item format in accordance with FAR Part 12 on or about December 1, 2026, with a tentative closing date of December 15, 2026. The NAICS code for this procurement is 325412. Any future amendments and other miscellaneous documents will be available electronically for download at SAM.gov. No paper copies of the solicitation will be available, and no telephone requests for paper copies of the solicitation will be accepted. Interested offerors are advised to continuously check Contracting Opportunities at SAM.gov for any changes to this solicitation. All responsible sources may submit an offer that if timely received, will be considered. The point of contact for this procurement is Jacob Werling. Questions can be e-mailed to Jacob.Werling@va.gov. title: INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT (LIMA, PERU): DAY 2 � CONSTRUCTION
description: US ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS (USACE) � LATIN AMERICA AND CARIBBEAN DISTRICT INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT: DAY 2 � CONSTRUCTION Requirement: Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization - Construction Customer Agency: Peruvian Navy Notice ID: W51DQV27Z1CV9 NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Associated Sources Sought: W51DQV27S1CQ0 Event Date: Wednesday, December 2, 2026 Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja, Lima, Peru RSVP Deadline: November 18, 2026, at 3:00 pm CT General Overview The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District, is hosting an Industry Day event in Lima, Peru, to engage with industry partners regarding the upcoming acquisition of the Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project and NAMRU-S O&M Project. To provide focused engagement for distinct industry sectors, the event is structured over three specialized days: Day 1 (Tuesday, December 1, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Architecture & Engineering (A/E) Services (NAICS 541330) Day 2 (Wednesday, December 2, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Construction (NAICS 236220) Day 3 (Thursday, December 3, 2026): U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) Lima and Iquitos, Peru - Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Services (NAICS 561210) This announcement specifically covers Day 2 (Construction). Separate announcements address Day 1 (A/E Services) and Day 3 Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M). Purpose of the Event The purpose is to present the planned Design-Build construction requirements for the shoreside modernization at Callao, brief prospective prime contractors and subcontractors on USACE contracting and technical standards, explain federal registration procedures, and conduct one-on-one market research capability briefings. Summary of the Sessions The program includes three distinct sessions: Construction: A comprehensive briefing on project scope, facility packages, technical specifications, procurement timelines, and USACE compliance requirements. One-on-One Capability Briefings: Private, scheduled 15-minute briefings reserved for prospective Prime Contractors to present capabilities directly to the USACE acquisition team. title: Tax Software and Support
description: The IRS has an ongoing requirement for commercial tax software products and associated services supporting the Federal Tax Compliance mission. The anticipated contract will provide software licenses, customization, software maintenance, integration, training, and user and technical support. The requirement includes, but is not limited to: Up to 130 Tax Analyzer licenses and annual renewals; Up to 150 Tax Planner licenses and annual renewals; Tax software user and technical support/help desk services; Maintenance of IRS-customized Issue Management System (IMS) Tax Engine Middleware; Support and maintenance of the Tax Engine Middleware Plug-In; Software customization and integration; Annual face-to-face training for up to 25 participants; Quarterly virtual training for licensed users; Software updates, upgrades, patches, and enhancements; Integration and testing support; and Associated program management, cybersecurity, documentation, and technical support services. Anticipated Period of Performance Base Period: December 18, 2026 - December 17, 2027 Option Period 1: December 18, 2027 - December 17, 2028 Option Period 2: December 18, 2028 - December 17, 2029 Option Period 3: December 18, 2029 - December 17, 2030 Option Period 4: December 18, 2030 - December 17, 2031 The government anticipates awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract utilizing a Best-Value Tradeoff (BVTO) source selection approach in accordance with FAR 15.101-1. Proposals will be evaluated based on the following factors, listed in descending order of importance: Technical Approach Licensing, Middleware Integration & Support Capability Past Performance Price The combined non-price factors are significantly more important than price. Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the government, considering price and non-price factors. The government intends to award without discussions; however, it reserves the right to conduct discussions if determined necessary by the Contracting Officer. Questions and Proposal Submission Questions Due: October 30, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Time. Proposals Due: November 18, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Time. All questions and proposals shall be submitted electronically via email to both: louis.c.browniii@irs.gov tanya.r.burnett@irs.gov Offerors shall submit proposals in accordance with Section L, Instructions, Conditions, and Notices to Offerors, and Section M, Evaluation Factors for Award, of the attached solicitation. Interested offerors are encouraged to carefully review the solicitation and all accompanying attachments for complete technical requirements, proposal instructions, evaluation criteria, and applicable terms and conditions. Any amendments, clarifications, or updates to this solicitation will be posted on SAM.gov. title: Austempered Ductile Iron (ADI) 5 Inch Projectile Bodies
description: The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), Contracts Department intends to issue a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract on a sole source basis to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation. The NAICS is 332993. The Contractor shall develop and produce new Austempered Ductile Iron (ADI) 5 Inch Projectile Bodies compatible with the MK 45 Gun Weapon System. In accordance with 10 USC �4022, the Government will be awarding a follow-on FAR contract. The Naval Energetic Systems and Technologies (NEST) Request for Prototype Projects (RPP), under which this prototype OTA was awarded, included provisions for a follow-on production contract. The prototype OTA award for the ADI 5 Inch Projectile Bodies development and qualification was competitively awarded and the associated tasks mentioned above were delivered successfully and accepted by the Government as the basis for the prototype build. The participant in the OTA (Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation) successfully completed the prototype projects provided for in N001742390042. As such, the requirements of 10 USC �4022(f)(1) and DFARS 206.001-70 have been met and a follow-on contract for production can proceed without further competition. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of 10 USC 4022(f)(1), as implemented in DFARS 206.001-70, Exception for prototype projects for follow-on production contracts. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals nor does it restrict the Government from an ultimate acquisition approach; however, the Government will consider all responses received to this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement is solely within the discretion of the Government. This notice should not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose. Requests for solicitation will not receive a response. All information is to be submitted at no cost or obligation to the U.S. Government. The U.S. Government reserves the right to reject, in whole or in part, any input as a result of this market survey. The U.S. Government is not obligated to notify respondents of the results of this survey. If a formal solicitation is generated at a later date, a solicitation notice will be published. All interested sources shall provide the organization name, address, point of contact, phone number, fax number, e-mail address, business size, taxpayer identification number, DUNS number, and CAGE Code. In addition, all interested sources shall provide a summary of their company�s capabilities. title: USS OKANE (DDG-77); 7MRB0604 Standalone
description: The Southwest Regional Maintenance Center (SWRMC) intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) No. N5523627R0007 for the execution of the Preservation, Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical/Electronic Repairs for USS OKANE (DDG-77) 7MRB0604.The Preservation, Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical/Electronic Repairs for USS OKANE (DDG-77) 7MRB0604 is anticipated to take approximately eleven (11) months beginning on January 25, 2027, through October 10, 2027. The repairs shall be performed at a contractors facility within a 50-mile radius of Naval Base San Diego. If the Navy issues a solicitation for the Preservation, Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical/Electronic Repairs, the acquisition and solicitation-to-award process shall abide by Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul, Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) and the Navy Marine Corps Acquisition Regulation Supplement (NMCARS) guidelines. The Government anticipates awarding this effort as a supply contract whereas the supply equates to the procurement of a repaired, mission-ready USS OKANE (DDG-77) 7MRB0604 to be returned to service to the Fleet. The anticipated scope of work includes all labor, supervision, production, testing and quality assurance necessary to prepare for and accomplish the Preservation, Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical/Electronic Repairs. The Navy will issue the solicitation electronically on https://piee.eb.mil and www.Sam.gov and interested parties must comply with that solicitation requirements and instructions for proposals. Interested offerors are hereby encouraged to monitor https://piee.eb.mil and www.Sam.gov for the anticipated release of the solicitation and any associated amendments. Offerors shall be registered in the Solicitation Module in Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) and System for Award Management (SAM) in order to be eligible for award. This synopsis is issued in accordance with FAR 5.101(a) and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not accept proposals as a result of this synopsis. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any questions submitted or information provided in response to this notice. The Government anticipates issuing a competitive Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) solicitation on November 18, 2026. The RFP will be a Total Small Business Set-Aside and the applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 336611, Ship Building and Repairing (a small business must have 1,300 or less employees).Offerors that are interested in this procurement may send an e-mail providing all point of contact information (company name and address, CAGE code, primary and secondary points of contact, telephone phone number, and e-mail addresses) to 410B_RFP_27R0007_OKN_RHIB@us.navy.mil and subsequently will receive a courtesy notification when the solicitation is posted.

One-on-One Capability Briefings: Private, scheduled 15-minute briefings reserved for prospective Prime Contractors to present capabilities directly to the USACE acquisition team. Federal Systems Registration Support: Individual, walk-in technical assistance to help prospective vendors navigate SAM.gov, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), NCAGE, and PIEE registration. Please note: This announcement is issued solely for market research and informational planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), an Invitation for Bids (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the U.S. Government. No contract award will result directly from this event.
