description: The Southwest Regional Maintenance Center (SWRMC) intends to issue Request for Proposal (RFP) No. N5523627R0007 for the execution of the Preservation, Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical/Electronic Repairs for USS OKANE (DDG-77) 7MRX0604.The Preservation, Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical/Electronic Repairs for USS OKANE (DDG-77) 7MRX0604 is anticipated to take approximately eleven (11) months beginning on January 25, 2027, through October 10, 2027. title: INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT (LIMA, PERU): DAY 1 � ARCHITECTURE & ENGINEERING (A/E) SERVICES
description: US ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS (USACE) � LATIN AMERICA AND CARIBBEAN DISTRICT INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT: DAY 1 � ARCHITECTURE & ENGINEERING (A/E) SERVICES Requirement: Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization - AE Customer Agency: Peruvian Navy Notice ID: W51DQV27Z1CV8 NAICS Code: 541330 � Engineering Services Event Date: Wednesday, December 1, 2026 Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja, Lima, Peru RSVP Deadline: November 18, 2026, at 3:00 pm CT General Overview The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Latin America & Caribbean District, is hosting an Industry Day event in Lima, Peru, to engage with industry partners regarding the upcoming acquisition of the Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project and NAMRU-S O&M Project. To provide focused engagement for distinct industry sectors, the event is structured over three specialized days: Day 1 (Tuesday, December 1, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Architecture & Engineering (A/E) Services (NAICS 541330) Day 2 (Wednesday, December 2, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Construction (NAICS 236220) Day 3 (Thursday, December 3, 2026): U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) Lima and Iquitos, Peru - Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Services (NAICS 561210) This announcement specifically covers Day 1 (A/E Services). Separate announcements address Day 2 (Construction) and Day 3 Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M). Purpose of the Event The purpose is to present the planned Architectural and Engineering (A/E) requirements in support of shoreside and port facility modernization at Callao Naval Base, brief prospective prime design firms and specialized consultants on USACE engineering criteria and U.S. Federal contracting standards, provide walk-in technical guidance on federal vendor registrations, and conduct private one-on-one market research capability briefings. Summary of the Sessions The program includes three distinct sessions: A/E Design: A comprehensive briefing detailing project scope, facility design packages, site conditions, host-nation and DoD design standards, BIM requirements, procurement timelines, and USACE compliance guidelines. One-on-One Capability Briefings: Private, scheduled 15-minute briefings reserved for prospective A/E firms to present specialized technical and managerial capabilities directly to the USACE acquisition panel. Federal Systems Registration Support: Individual, walk-in technical assistance to help prospective firms navigate SAM.gov, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and NCAGE. Please note: This announcement is issued solely for market research and informational planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), an Invitation for Bids (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the U.S. Government. No contract award will result directly from this event. Logistics & Schedule Date: December 1, 2026 Hours: 08:30 � 4:00 PM CT/Local Lima Time Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja Av. San Luis S/N� Cdra. 24, Urb. San Borja Sur, Lima, Peru Daily Schedule Note: A detailed schedule of presentations, networking intervals, and allocated session times is currently being finalized. The specific daily agenda will be published in a forthcoming update to this announcement prior to the event. Event Details & Specific Sessions Session 1: A/E Seminar & Design Scope Briefing USACE engineering, project management, and contracting representatives will deliver a detailed technical presentation covering: Master planning, site layout, and architectural vision for the Callao Naval Base modernization. Design criteria, geotechnical and seismic considerations, coastal environment durability standards, and Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC). Building Information Modeling (BIM), specialized mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP), fire protection, environmental permitting, and host-nation building codes. Overview of the federal A/E Brooks Act selection process (FAR Part 36.6), evaluation criteria, submission requirements (Standard Form 330), and milestone schedules. Session 2: One-on-One Capability Briefings (Pre-Registration Required) Prospective A/E firms (including formal Joint Ventures and Prime Mentor-Prot�g� partnerships) may request a dedicated 15-minute private session with the USACE technical and acquisition panel. Objective: Market research to assess industry interest, multi-disciplinary engineering depth, regional design experience, BIM/CADD capabilities, and past performance. Availability: Time slots are limited and will be confirmed on a strictly first-come, first-served basis upon receipt and validation of the RSVP form. Session 3: Federal Systems Registration Support Throughout the day, USACE specialists will host an individual support station to assist contractors with: Firms interested in receiving support should bring a computer Navigating NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code applications. Obtaining a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and activating an account in SAM.gov. Project & Requirement Overview Project Description The contemplated acquisition covers comprehensive multi-disciplinary Architecture and Engineering (A/E) services. The scope of work encompasses: Topographic, hydrographic, and geotechnical site investigations and soil stabilization analysis. Comprehensive seismic engineering compliant with Peruvian seismic zones and DoD structural criteria. Concept development, 35% preliminary design, 65% intermediate design, and final 100% ready-to-advertise design packages and technical specifications. Multi-discipline engineering including civil, structural, architectural, MEP, specialized fire suppression, industrial ventilation, cold-chain refrigeration, and telecommunications. Environmental assessments, stormwater management planning, and host-nation regulatory compliance support. Complete Furniture, Fixtures, & Equipment (FF&E) interior design packages. Development of construction cost estimates (MII format) and construction phasing schedules. Summary of Facility Packages: Building 110 Primary Function: Spare Parts Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Heavy-duty slab design, industrial racking integration, material handling flow, automated logistics staging. Building 115 Primary Function: Clothing & Gear Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: High-density pallet storage, humidity and climate control, inventory distribution bays. Building 112 Primary Function: Material Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Bulk staging, overhead crane/hoist accommodations, heavy equipment ingress/egress ramps. Building 113 Primary Function: Customs Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Secure bonded holding areas, host-nation customs inspection layout, physical security infrastructure. Building 114 Primary Function: Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Secondary containment, explosion-proof electrical systems, specialized foam/water fire suppression, environmental drainage controls. Building 111 Primary Function: Medicine & Medical Supplies Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Temperature/humidity-controlled storage (cold chain capability), pharmaceutical-grade clean finishings, backup power integration. Building 120 Primary Function: DIRNOTEMAT & Quality Control Building Key Technical Considerations: Administrative offices, testing and quality inspection laboratories, specialized testing benches, IT/telecom infrastructure. Site & Ancillary Works Primary Function: Infrastructure & Integration Key Technical Considerations: Site grading, structural fill, perimeter security, access roads, utility connections, complete FF&E packages, and host-nation compliant permitting. Streamlined RSVP & Venue Access Instructions Due to facility capacity constraints and military installation security protocols at Centro Naval, advance registration is mandatory. title: Greece – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – «Παροχή Υπηρεσιών Συντήρησης, Υποστήριξης και παραμετροποίησης του Πληροφοριακού Συστήματος Μηχανισμού Πληρωμών Προγραμμάτων Επιδοτήσεων (Escrow Accounts) της Κοινωνίας της Πληροφορίας Μ.Α.Ε.».
description: Αντικείμενο του έργου είναι η παροχή υπηρεσιών συντήρησης, τεχνικής και λειτουργικής υποστήριξης, καθώς και παραμετροποίησης του Πληροφοριακού Συστήματος Μηχανισμού Πληρωμών μέσω Escrow Accounts της Κοινωνίας της Πληροφορίας Μ.Α.Ε., με στόχο τη διασφάλιση της απρόσκοπτης, ασφαλούς και αποδοτικής λειτουργίας του και την υποστήριξη της ένταξης νέων έργων, δράσεων και χρηματοδοτικών προγραμμάτων. Το έργο διαρθρώνεται σε δύο βασικές ενότητες εργασιών: Α. Συντήρηση και υποστήριξη του Πληροφοριακού Συστήματος: Περιλαμβάνει τη διαχείριση και επίλυση τεχνικών προβλημάτων, σφαλμάτων και περιστατικών (Bugs και Incidents), τον συντονισμό των εμπλεκόμενων τεχνικών και επιχειρησιακών ομάδων, τη διενέργεια ελέγχων ποιότητας και δοκιμών αποδοχής (UAT), καθώς και την παρακολούθηση της διαθεσιμότητας, της απόδοσης και της ορθής λειτουργίας της πλατφόρμας. Επιπλέον, περιλαμβάνει την παροχή υπηρεσιών Helpdesk και υποστήριξης χρηστών, την υποστήριξη των διαδικασιών πληρωμών σε συνεργασία με τα αρμόδια πιστωτικά ιδρύματα, τη διαχείριση ζητημάτων που αφορούν ρόλους και δικαιώματα πρόσβασης, την εφαρμογή ενημερώσεων ασφαλείας και διορθωτικών αναβαθμίσεων, την επικαιροποίηση εγχειριδίων χρήσης, την παρουσίαση των λειτουργιών του συστήματος και τη μεταφορά τεχνογνωσίας. Στο πλαίσιο αυτό, προβλέπεται επίσης η παρακολούθηση και αξιοποίηση στοιχείων υποστήριξης μέσω Jira και η παραγωγή αναφορών και επιχειρησιακών δεικτών μέσω Microsoft Power BI. Β. Παραμετροποίηση και ένταξη νέων έργων και δράσεων: Περιλαμβάνει την ανάλυση και καταγραφή των επιχειρησιακών απαιτήσεων κάθε νέου έργου ή δράσης, την παραμετροποίηση και προσαρμογή των υφιστάμενων λειτουργιών της πλατφόρμας, τη διαμόρφωση ρόλων, δικαιωμάτων, ροών εργασίας, διαδικασιών ελέγχου και έγκρισης, καθώς και των απαιτούμενων στοιχείων, διασυνδέσεων και αναφορών. Επιπλέον, περιλαμβάνει τη διενέργεια τεχνικών και λειτουργικών δοκιμών, την υποστήριξη της παραγωγικής ενεργοποίησης κάθε νέας δράσης, την επικαιροποίηση της σχετικής τεκμηρίωσης, τη μεταφορά τεχνογνωσίας και τον συντονισμό των εμπλεκόμενων φορέων έως την ολοκλήρωση της ένταξης. [παρ. 1.3 & ΠΑΡΑΡΤΗΜΑ I της Διακήρυξης]

title: MACH1_AOI_FA890327M1006_F-47 Future Campus at Nellis AFB
description: **Update 12 Nov 2026**: Added Attachment Q&A (Final Round) **Update 5 Nov 2026**: Added Attachment Q&A (First Round) **Update 1 Nov 2026**: Added Attachment F, Proposed Construction Markups and Commercial Pricing Perameters MACH1 Area of Interest: F-47 Future Campus at Nellis AFB, Rapid Delivery Progressive Design-Build The 772d Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS), in coordination with the Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC), is seeking highly qualified Design-Build teams to deliver the Rapid Delivery Projects supporting the F-47 mission at Nellis Air Force Base, Nevada, utilizing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model. This Area of Interest (AOI) is issued under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice, FA8903-OT-MACH1. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Respondents shall comply with the MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice and the project-specific requirements established in the attached AOI. Program Overview The F-47 Campus at Nellis AFB is an approximately $1.057 billion total programmed military construction initiative intended to provide the facilities and infrastructure necessary to support the F-47 mission. This amount includes construction, contingency, design, construction security, and other applicable project costs and does not represent the construction agreement value available under this AOI. The present acquisition contemplates award for the Rapid Delivery Projects under Milestones 2 through 4 only, consisting of: Combined Operations and Maintenance Hangar. Reprogramming Laboratory. Simulator Facility. Aircraft Apron with Sunshades. Supporting utilities and infrastructure necessary for permanent operation of the Rapid Delivery facilities. The Government strongly prefers to select one Design-Build team capable of delivering all Rapid Delivery Projects, while reserving the right to select up to four teams if warranted by program requirements and permitted by the applicable acquisition authority. The Government also values organizations possessing the qualifications and resources to support the remaining Nellis F-47 Campus. However, selection under this AOI does not guarantee Milestone 5 or subsequent Agreement(s). Progressive Design-Build Delivery Approach The Government intends to initiate design and preconstruction services following completion of the Planning Charrette Reports establishing the initial mission requirements. The selected Design-Build team will work collaboratively with AFCEC and its Owner's Advisor to advance facility designs, evaluate alternative technical and construction solutions, develop cost and schedule strategies, and establish commercially supportable construction pricing. The Government contemplates negotiating firm-fixed-price construction agreement at approximately 65% design completion, subject to sufficient scope maturity, risk allocation, and commercial cost viability. Advanced design packages, early construction activities, and long-lead procurement may be considered where appropriately justified and authorized. AFCEC seeks a collaborative construction partner committed to delivering the greatest possible mission capability and value for the resources invested. The Government intends to consider innovative design and construction approaches, including industrialized construction methods, commercially effective Agreement commitment strategies, and practical alternatives that improve affordability and schedule performance. Three-Phase Selection Process The Government intends to conduct an expedited three-phase selection process under MACH1: Phase 1: Solution Brief. Respondents will submit qualifications and technical information demonstrating the capabilities of their actual proposed design and construction organizations. The attached AOI establishes ten project-specific technical factors and a maximum of 20 narrative pages, with separately permitted appendices. No construction price or rough-order-of-magnitude construction estimate is required during Phase 1 Submissions. Phase 2: Oral Presentations / Pitch Sessions. Selected respondents will be invited to participate in oral presentations. Detailed instructions and additional technical information will be provided to invited respondents, subject to applicable information-security requirements. Phase 3: Full Phase 3 Submission and Negotiations. The Government intends to conduct direct negotiations with selected respondent(s), subject to applicable authority and Agreements Officer approval. Commercial viability of the price will be evaluated before award. Anticipated Acquisition Schedule AOI Release: October 30, 2026. Initial Industry Questions Due: November 4, 2026. Final Industry Questions Due: November 10, 2026. Phase 1 Solution Briefs Due: November 18, 2026, at 9:00 PM Central Standard Time. Phase 2 Invitations: By December 2, 2026. Phase 2 Oral Presentations: December 14�17, 2026. Phase 3 Invitations: December 22, 2026. Phase 3 Submissions Due: January 15, 2027. Target Initial OTA Award: February 5, 2027. All dates are anticipated and subject to revision by the Agreements Officer. Submission Instructions Respondents shall review the complete attached AOI and MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice for eligibility requirements, technical factors, page limits, qualification-sheet requirements, cybersecurity provisions, and evaluation procedures. Phase 1 submissions shall be unclassified and submitted as a single searchable PDF with the required bookmarks and appendices. Submit Solution Briefs electronically to: 772ESS.PKA.MACH1@us.af.mil Reference the assigned Nellis F-47 Campus AOI Notice ID in the email subject line. All questions and acquisition communications shall be directed to the Agreements Officer through the designated MACH1 correspondence address. Only authorized Government officials may modify AOI requirements or make commitments binding upon the Government. The Government reserves the right to amend or cancel this AOI, request supplemental information, limit the number of respondents advancing to subsequent phases, or make no award, consistent with applicable authority. The attached AOI establishes the controlling project-specific submission requirements and evaluation procedures.

The Government contemplates negotiating firm-fixed-price construction agreement at approximately 65% design completion, subject to sufficient scope maturity, risk allocation, and commercial cost viability. Advanced design packages, early construction activities, and long-lead procurement may be considered where appropriately justified and authorized. AFCEC seeks a collaborative construction partner committed to delivering the greatest possible mission capability and value for the resources invested. The Government intends to consider innovative design and construction approaches, including industrialized construction methods, commercially effective Agreement commitment strategies, and practical alternatives that improve affordability and schedule performance. Three-Phase Selection Process The Government intends to conduct an expedited three-phase selection process under MACH1: Phase 1: Solution Brief. Respondents will submit qualifications and technical information demonstrating the capabilities of their actual proposed design and construction organizations. The attached AOI establishes ten project-specific technical factors and a maximum of 20 narrative pages, with separately permitted appendices. No construction price or rough-order-of-magnitude construction estimate is required during Phase 1 Submissions. Phase 2: Oral Presentations / Pitch Sessions. Selected respondents will be invited to participate in oral presentations. Detailed instructions and additional technical information will be provided to invited respondents, subject to applicable information-security requirements. Phase 3: Full Phase 3 Submission and Negotiations. The Government intends to conduct direct negotiations with selected respondent(s), subject to applicable authority and Agreements Officer approval. Commercial viability of the price will be evaluated before award. Anticipated Acquisition Schedule AOI Release: October 30, 2026. Initial Industry Questions Due: November 4, 2026. Final Industry Questions Due: November 10, 2026. Phase 1 Solution Briefs Due: November 18, 2026, at 9:00 PM Central Standard Time. Phase 2 Invitations: By December 2, 2026. Phase 2 Oral Presentations: December 14�17, 2026. Phase 3 Invitations: December 22, 2026. Phase 3 Submissions Due: January 15, 2027. Target Initial OTA Award: February 5, 2027. All dates are anticipated and subject to revision by the Agreements Officer. Submission Instructions Respondents shall review the complete attached AOI and MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice for eligibility requirements, technical factors, page limits, qualification-sheet requirements, cybersecurity provisions, and evaluation procedures. Phase 1 submissions shall be unclassified and submitted as a single searchable PDF with the required bookmarks and appendices. Submit Solution Briefs electronically to: 772ESS.PKA.MACH1@us.af.mil Reference the assigned Nellis F-47 Campus AOI Notice ID in the email subject line. All questions and acquisition communications shall be directed to the Agreements Officer through the designated MACH1 correspondence address. Only authorized Government officials may modify AOI requirements or make commitments binding upon the Government. The Government reserves the right to amend or cancel this AOI, request supplemental information, limit the number of respondents advancing to subsequent phases, or make no award, consistent with applicable authority. The attached AOI establishes the controlling project-specific submission requirements and evaluation procedures.

Rack breakers out for physical inspection. Perform mechanical integrity inspection (linkages, springs, shutters, rails). Evaluate relay configuration: GE Multilin F-60, G-30, MIF II, UR-series relays, ABB relays. Review protective relay event logs. Verify battery health for control relays. Inspect control wiring and MOC/TOC blocks. Document all deficiencies discovered. Repair Tasks: Replace trip coils/close coils where improper voltages or failures are found. Replace or repair MOC/TOC blocks. Replace relay control batteries. Repair/replace defective relays (G-30, Multilin series, if field-repairable, ABB). Correct wiring faults, loose lugs, damaged insulation. ATS logic troubleshooting and repair (ASCO control board testing, timing sequence validation, mechanical). Functional testing of each breaker after repair. Re-racking, lubrication, cleaning, and cabinet maintenance Generator/ATS Integration Testing (as needed) Support load-bank verification of generator response (coordination with CAT dealer). Remove/reconnect bias signals during generator tuning (if required). Deliverables Investigation Report identifying all deficiencies. Repair Completion Report summarizing corrective actions performed. Updated device condition log for the switchgear, ATS units, and relays. Recommendations for future reliability improvements. It is the responsibility of the quoter to submit sufficient information to convey their technical capability in meeting the requirements of the Statement of Work. Failure to provide sufficient information will result in the quote being considered not technically acceptable. 7. Provide a list of three (3) other concerns and/or Government agencies for which services similar in size and scope were rendered by the Offeror over the past three years. title: MACH1_AOI_FA890327M1006_F-47 Future Campus at Nellis AFB
description: **Update 5 Nov 2026**: Added First Round Q&A Matrix **Update 1 Nov 2026**: Added Attachment F, Proposed Construction Markups and Commercial Pricing Perameters MACH1 Area of Interest: F-47 Future Campus at Nellis AFB, Rapid Delivery Progressive Design-Build The 772d Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS), in coordination with the Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC), is seeking highly qualified Design-Build teams to deliver the Rapid Delivery Projects supporting the F-47 mission at Nellis Air Force Base, Nevada, utilizing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model. This Area of Interest (AOI) is issued under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice, FA8903-OT-MACH1. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Respondents shall comply with the MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice and the project-specific requirements established in the attached AOI. Program Overview The F-47 Campus at Nellis AFB is an approximately $1.057 billion total programmed military construction initiative intended to provide the facilities and infrastructure necessary to support the F-47 mission. This amount includes construction, contingency, design, construction security, and other applicable project costs and does not represent the construction agreement value available under this AOI. The present acquisition contemplates award for the Rapid Delivery Projects under Milestones 2 through 4 only, consisting of: Combined Operations and Maintenance Hangar. Reprogramming Laboratory. Simulator Facility. Aircraft Apron with Sunshades. Supporting utilities and infrastructure necessary for permanent operation of the Rapid Delivery facilities. The Government strongly prefers to select one Design-Build team capable of delivering all Rapid Delivery Projects, while reserving the right to select up to four teams if warranted by program requirements and permitted by the applicable acquisition authority. The Government also values organizations possessing the qualifications and resources to support the remaining Nellis F-47 Campus. However, selection under this AOI does not guarantee Milestone 5 or subsequent Agreement(s). Progressive Design-Build Delivery Approach The Government intends to initiate design and preconstruction services following completion of the Planning Charrette Reports establishing the initial mission requirements. The selected Design-Build team will work collaboratively with AFCEC and its Owner's Advisor to advance facility designs, evaluate alternative technical and construction solutions, develop cost and schedule strategies, and establish commercially supportable construction pricing. The Government contemplates negotiating firm-fixed-price construction agreement at approximately 65% design completion, subject to sufficient scope maturity, risk allocation, and commercial cost viability. Advanced design packages, early construction activities, and long-lead procurement may be considered where appropriately justified and authorized. AFCEC seeks a collaborative construction partner committed to delivering the greatest possible mission capability and value for the resources invested. The Government intends to consider innovative design and construction approaches, including industrialized construction methods, commercially effective Agreement commitment strategies, and practical alternatives that improve affordability and schedule performance. Three-Phase Selection Process The Government intends to conduct an expedited three-phase selection process under MACH1: Phase 1: Solution Brief. Respondents will submit qualifications and technical information demonstrating the capabilities of their actual proposed design and construction organizations. The attached AOI establishes ten project-specific technical factors and a maximum of 20 narrative pages, with separately permitted appendices. No construction price or rough-order-of-magnitude construction estimate is required during Phase 1 Submissions. Phase 2: Oral Presentations / Pitch Sessions. Selected respondents will be invited to participate in oral presentations. Detailed instructions and additional technical information will be provided to invited respondents, subject to applicable information-security requirements. Phase 3: Full Phase 3 Submission and Negotiations. The Government intends to conduct direct negotiations with selected respondent(s), subject to applicable authority and Agreements Officer approval. Commercial viability of the price will be evaluated before award. Anticipated Acquisition Schedule AOI Release: October 30, 2026. Initial Industry Questions Due: November 4, 2026. Final Industry Questions Due: November 10, 2026. Phase 1 Solution Briefs Due: November 18, 2026, at 9:00 PM Central Standard Time. Phase 2 Invitations: By December 2, 2026. Phase 2 Oral Presentations: December 14�17, 2026. Phase 3 Invitations: December 22, 2026. Phase 3 Submissions Due: January 15, 2027. Target Initial OTA Award: February 5, 2027. All dates are anticipated and subject to revision by the Agreements Officer. Submission Instructions Respondents shall review the complete attached AOI and MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice for eligibility requirements, technical factors, page limits, qualification-sheet requirements, cybersecurity provisions, and evaluation procedures. Phase 1 submissions shall be unclassified and submitted as a single searchable PDF with the required bookmarks and appendices. Submit Solution Briefs electronically to: 772ESS.PKA.MACH1@us.af.mil Reference the assigned Nellis F-47 Campus AOI Notice ID in the email subject line. All questions and acquisition communications shall be directed to the Agreements Officer through the designated MACH1 correspondence address. Only authorized Government officials may modify AOI requirements or make commitments binding upon the Government. The Government reserves the right to amend or cancel this AOI, request supplemental information, limit the number of respondents advancing to subsequent phases, or make no award, consistent with applicable authority. The attached AOI establishes the controlling project-specific submission requirements and evaluation procedures.

title: Requirement to support the Formerly Used Defense Sites (FUDS) Program Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC)
description: This Sources Sought announcement is for market research purposes only and should not be construed as a solicitation. There is no entitlement to payment by the Government of direct or indirect costs or charges that arise as a result of the submission of information in response to this request for information (RFI). The Government shall not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for any improperly identified proprietary information. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Savannah District is considering the solicitation and subsequent award of a Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) in support of the Formerly Used Defense Sites (FUDS) program. This requirement is for comprehensive support for the Formerly Used Defense Sites (FUDS) Program. The draft SOW defines the scope of program management, administrative, logistical, and community relations services necessary to execute and document FUDS projects. The range of activities includes maintaining and updating the FUDSMIS database, ensuring project documentation remains current, supporting Project Managers in developing and revising Project Management Plans and Site Management Action Plans, records management, preparation and coordination of key project documents, document uploads to the FUDS Documents portal, Cost-to-Complete estimate processes, logistics and community outreach support (including PDT and public meetings, Restoration Advisory Board activities, fact sheets, ROEs, and Section 508-compliant materials), and identification and implementation of efficiencies and streamlining measures. The Contractor shall undertake these support activities to achieve program objectives across FUDS projects and sites. Submission Instructions: Please follow the link below to access the survey.

title: Netherlands – Canteen and catering services – EA Cateringvoorzieningen
description: De aan te besteden Opdracht betreft de verzorging van de cateringvoorzieningen in de in de volgende paragraaf genoemde locaties. Onder deze voorzieningen behoren: - De verkoop van eten en drinken aan studenten en medewerkers in uitgiftepunten - Verzorgen van banqueting in de vorm van onder andere: • vergader- en lunchservices • avondmaaltijden • evenementen - De exploitatie van vendingautomaten Het gaat hierbij om 9 locaties, echter zal een belangrijke ontwikkeling betreffende de transformatie en uitbreiding van de locatie aan de Wandelboslaan 1 tot Campus Wandelbos plaatsvinden. Op deze campus worden verschillende mbo-opleidingen en ondersteunende diensten van Yonder samengebracht. Naar verwachting zullen circa 1.300 studenten en 425 medewerkers gebruikmaken van deze locatie. Een deel van hen volgt een BBL-opleiding en is daardoor niet dagelijks op de campus aanwezig. Campus Wandelbos wordt voorzien van een restaurant voor studenten en medewerkers. De oplevering is voorzien in december 2026, waarna de eerste lessen volgens de huidige planning in januari 2027 plaatsvinden. Daarnaast worden de gebouwen en de buitenruimte van Campus Stappegoor in de periode 2026–2030 gefaseerd vernieuwd en verduurzaamd. De werkzaamheden kunnen tijdelijk of structureel gevolgen hebben voor studenten- en medewerkersstromen, de bereikbaarheid en beschikbaarheid van cateringvoorzieningen en de wijze waarop de dienstverlening op deze campus wordt georganiseerd. Naar verwachting zullen circa 3.000 studenten en 475 medewerkers gebruikmaken van deze locatie.

title: Germany – General construction work for pipelines – Lieferung und Montage von GFK-Rohrleitungen (DN 2000 / 2200) - Projekt Flusswärmepumpe 3 Mannheim
description: Die MVV Flusswärme GmbH (Tochterunternehmen der MVV Energie AG) (MVV) plant am Standort der Großkraftwerk Mannheim AG (GKM) in Mannheim-Neckarau die Errichtung und den Betrieb einer Flusswasser-Wärmepumpenanlage (WPA3) mit einer Heizleistung von bis zu 120 MWth. Dabei wird der Rhein als Wärmequelle über die bestehende Kühlwasserinfrastruktur des GKM und neu zu verlegende GFK-Rohrleitungen (DN 2000 / 2200) an die Wärmepumpenanlage angebunden. Die Ausschreibung umfasst die Planung, Lieferung und betriebsfertige Montage von GFK-Rohrleitungen sowie die dazugehörigen Tiefbauarbeiten. Zu den Planungsaufgaben zählen unter anderem Rohrleitungsberechnungen, Isometrien, Rohrstatiken, Kollisionsprüfungen sowie die Erstellung von Abnahmeprotokollen und Fertigungsunterlagen. Der Leistungsumfang beinhaltet die Installation von DN 2000- und DN 2200-GFK-Rohrleitungen, die Errichtung eines Kraftschlussbeckens im Rohrleitungsverlauf, den temporären Rückbau und Neubau bestehender Entwässerungsleitungen DN 400 bis DN 800 aus Beton / Stahlbeton sowie Aushub-, Verfüll- und Wiederherstellungsarbeiten. Die durchzuführenden Arbeiten sind unter Berücksichtigung der betrieblichen Abläufe der GKM abschnittsweise auszuführen.

title: Germany – Joinery and carpentry installation work – Anna-Susanna-Stieg 3 - Tischler Einbaumöbel
description: SBH | Schulbau Hamburg hat als Landesbetrieb der Freien und Hansestadt Hamburg (nachstehend SBH genannt) die Aufgabe, die Schulimmobilien unter Berücksichtigung der schulischen Belange nach wirtschaftlichen Grundsätzen zu planen, zu bauen, zu unterhalten und zu bewirtschaften und die mehr als 400 Schulen an die Behörde für Schule und Berufsbildung (BSB) zu vermieten. --------------- Die Grundschule Anna-Susanna-Stieg wird um ein multifunktionales Klassengebäude mit Mensa, Vitalküche und Einfeldsporthalle ergänzt. Der Neubau würde dabei erstmals die Bildung von mindestens fünfzügigen Jahrgangszentren ermöglichen. Im Osten schließt sich der neue, zentrale Schulhof an und im Süden sowie zwischen den Sporthallen sind die Außensportflächen vorgesehen. --------------- Hier: Tischler Einbaumöbel --------------- Bei den zu erbringenden Leistungen handelt es sich um Tischlerarbeiten für die Werkplanung, Fertigung, Lieferung und Montage von maßgefertigten Einbaumöbeln in Schulgebäuden. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst die Erstellung der Werkplanung nach örtlichem Aufmaß sowie die Herstellung und Montage verschiedener Möbel- und Ausstattungselemente aus Holzwerkstoffen einschließlich aller erforderlichen Beschläge, Oberflächenbehandlungen, Polsterungen, Befestigungen und Anpassungsarbeiten. Die Leistungen werden schlüsselfertig bis zur betriebsbereiten Übergabe erbracht.

title: Germany – Building construction work – Stadt Bochum: Totalunternehmer / Totalübernehmer Grundschule in der Vöde, Castroper Str. 235
description: Die Stadt Bochum (nachfolgend "Auftraggeber") steht als Schulträger vor der Herausforderung, dem stetig wachsenden Raumbedarf aufgrund der steigenden Schulanmeldungen im Bochumer Stadtgebiet zu entsprechen. In diesem Zusammenhang herrscht - neben dem Erfordernis an Sanierungs- und Erhaltungsmaßnahmen bereits bestehender Schulgebäude - ein erheblicher Bedarf an der Schaffung neuer Sport- und Lernräume. Dabei ist der Auftraggeber nach dem Schulgesetz verpflichtet, Schulentwicklungsplanung zu betreiben. Zur Erfüllung dieser ihr gesetzlich obliegenden Pflicht plant der Auftraggeber dem wachsenden Raumbedarf im Rahmen eines umfassenden Schulbau- und Schulmodernisierungsprogramm zu begegnen. Dieses beinhaltet erforderliche Neubau-, Umbau- und Sanierungsmaßnahmen für 27 schulische Einrichtungen. Das Programm umfasst dabei alle Schularten und bezieht sich auf Grund-, Förder- und weiterführende Schulen. Eingebettet in dieses Schulbauprogramm soll nun die Erweiterung und der Umbau der Grundschule in der Vöde, Castroper Str. 235, 44791 Bochum erfolgen. Die bauliche Erweiterung sowie der Umbau der Grundschule in der Vöde nebst vorgelagertem Rückbau der Bestandsbauung soll durch einen Totalunternehmer / Totalübernehmer erfolgen. Die Grundschule in der Voede ist eine zweizügige Schule im Stadtteil Grumme. Die vorhandene Schüleranzahl von ca. 235 SuS (SJ 2026/27) wird bis zum Schuljahr 2030/31 auf prognostizierte 240 SuS anwachsen. Auf dem Grundstück befindet sich das Schulgebäude (ca. 468 m²), eine Trafostation (ca. 65 m²), eine Turnhalle (ca. 565 m²), die ehemalige Hausmeisterwohnung, die nun als OGS genutzt wird (ca. 132 m²) und ein an die Halle angebautes weiteres OGS-Gebäude (ca. 195 m²). Die Schulhoffläche beträgt ca. 2.100 m². Die geplante Maßnahme soll in drei Schritten realisiert werden: Schritt 1: Umbau Computerraum zu einem Klassenraum - bereits erfolgt; Ein Computerraum, der nicht mehr benötigt wurde, wurde zu einem Klassenraum umgebaut. Schritt 2: Containeranlage als zusätzlicher Klassenraum - bereits erfolgt; Ein Container vor dem Hauptgebäude an der Castroper Straße bietet Platz für einen weiteren Raum. Schritt 3: Rückbau des bestehenden Anbaus an die Turnhalle (OGS), Neubau und Umbau auf dem Schulhof (SJ 2030/31); Entlang der westlichen Grundstücksgrenze ist die Errichtung eines dreigeschossigen Neubaus vorgesehen. Da die nutzbare Schulhoffläche während der Bauphase erheblich eingeschränkt wird, soll der bestehende Anbau an die Turnhalle (Räumlichkeiten der OGS) vor der Ausführung des Neubaus zurückgebaut werden. Die entsprechenden Räume sollen im zweiten Obergeschoss des Neubaus untergebracht werden. Nach Abschluss der Neubauarbeiten erfolgen die erforderlichen Umbaumaßnahmen im Bestandsgebäude.
